item.stem:
Omar looks at the diagram of $\triangle PQR$ with $\angle P = 55^{\circ}$ and $\angle PQR = 65^{\circ}$. Side $PQ$ is extended to $S$, so $\angle RQS = x$.

Which claim finds $x$ correctly?

options.A: $x = 115^{\circ}$, because $\angle PQR = 65^{\circ}$ and $x$ forms a straight line with that interior angle.
options.B: $x = 65^{\circ}$, treating the interior $\angle PQR$ as if it were already the exterior angle.
options.C: Extending $PQ$ to $S$ is what creates $\angle P = 55^{\circ}$.
options.D: $x = 115^{\circ}$ by naming the triangle vertices alone, with no straight-angle step.
